prompt: What's the real reason to scope a capstone idea down to a one-week v1 instead of building the full ambitious vision right away?
choices: Smaller projects look more impressive on a resume
A finished small thing teaches you more than an unfinished ambitious one, and finishing is the actual skill being practiced
Big projects can't be tested with pytest
Employers only evaluate line count

prompt: In the habit tracker's scoping table, which feature gets cut first from the one-week v1?
choices: Marking a habit done for today
Multi-user accounts with login and cloud sync
Saving data so it survives between runs
Printing results to the terminal

prompt: Why does `cmd_log` check whether today's date is already in the habit's list before appending it?
choices: To prevent running the command twice in one day from creating a duplicate, inflated check-in count
To make the JSON file load faster
Because argparse requires a uniqueness check
To satisfy a Python syntax rule about lists

prompt: How should you think about this track's own DS&A content during this tier?
choices: It fully replaces the need to ever study algorithms in depth
It's a fast, light, intuition-first primer for this track's own interview-prep thread -- real depth on data structures and algorithms lives in the CS Foundations track
It's optional busywork that doesn't connect to the capstones
It only covers Big-O notation and nothing else

prompt: What data structure holds the list of check-in dates for a single habit in `habit.py`, and why does it fit?
choices: A single boolean, because you only need to know if today was logged
A list of ISO date strings, because you need an ordered, appendable, sortable collection of simple values
A nested class hierarchy, because habits need object-oriented modeling
A set of integers, because dates are best represented as numbers

prompt: In `test_log_does_not_duplicate_same_day`, why does the test call `habit.cmd_log(Args("reading"))` twice before asserting?
choices: To verify idempotency: logging the same habit twice in one day should not create two entries
To measure how fast the function runs
To simulate two different users logging the same habit
Because pytest requires every function to be called at least twice

prompt: According to the lesson's definition of done, what must be true for the v1 to count as genuinely finished?
choices: It must have at least 90% unit test coverage measured by a coverage tool
It must run end to end on a fresh clone, with a README, not just work on your own machine with leftover state
It must use a database instead of a flat file
It must include a graphical user interface

prompt: Why do the tests use `monkeypatch.setattr(habit, "DATA_FILE", tmp_path / "habits.json")` instead of letting tests write to the real habits.json?
choices: So each test starts from a clean, isolated file and can't corrupt or depend on your real data
Because JSON files can only be opened once per program run
To make the test suite run in a separate process
Because argparse requires all file paths to be set with monkeypatch
